free_text_reference_inventory.text: | **Astemizole Overdose**    | >100 mg (therapeutic range: 10–30 mg/day) oral; single or repeated ingestion | **Torsades de pointes (TdP), QT prolongation, cardiac arrest** (FDA 1999; EMA 2001). Fatalities reported at doses ≥100 mg (e.g., 120 mg/day in a 12-year-old) (Martinez-Rubio et al., 1993). |

| **Astemizole–Ketoconazole (Recommended Dose)** | Astemizole 10 mg/day + ketoconazole 200–400 mg/day (CYP3A4 inhibitor) | **Markedly prolonged QT interval, TdP, sudden death** (FDA Drug Safety Communication, 1999; EMA CPMP opinion, 2000). Cases included co-administration with other CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., erythromycin) (Honig et al., 1993). |
- **Overdose**: Clear dose-dependent cardiotoxicity (TdP risk increases with plasma levels >10 ng/mL; fatal cases at >50 ng/mL) (Woosley et al., 1993).
- **Interaction**: **Pharmacokinetic interaction** (ketoconazole inhibits CYP3A4-mediated metabolism), leading to **prolonged QT without overdose** (Honig et al., 1993).
- **Overdose**: Rapid onset (within hours) of syncope, palpitations, or sudden death; often in children or intentional ingestions (Martinez-Rubio et al., 1993).
- **Interaction**: Variability in ketoconazole metabolism (CYP3A4 polymorphisms) affects astemizole exposure (Thummel et al., 1996).
